reader.decision: Yes. Aelita implements the streaming change in app/exports.py, first checking what ferngrove.web.Response and ferngrove.db actually support, and adapting to them. If either lacks the needed API, Aelita stops and reports back instead of switching to another alternative on its own.
reader.decision_reason: The message identifies the root cause (the first byte waits for the whole export, so edge-lb idles out at 30s) and streaming fixes it without adding components. The only open risk is whether the unverified ferngrove APIs support iterators and cursors, which Aelita can check while implementing.

reconstruction.problem: export_contacts in app/exports.py loads all rows, builds the whole CSV in a StringIO, and only then returns it. For bluefin-logistics (412880 rows) this takes 89 seconds with no bytes sent. edge-lb closes the connection after 30 idle seconds and returns 504. The worker keeps building for 77 more seconds and the result is discarded. Small tenants such as harrow-dental (3120 rows, 1 second) work.
reconstruction.what_breaks: CSV export returns 504 for large tenants. The export is also close to the gunicorn 120-second timeout, so a larger tenant will hit that limit next.
reconstruction.fix: Return a streaming response: yield the CSV header immediately, then yield rows in batches of about 1000 from a DB cursor, so each chunk resets edge-lb's idle timer.
reconstruction.cost: Moderate code change in app/exports.py, no new components. Risks: ferngrove.web.Response may not accept an iterator and ferngrove.db may have no cursor (both unverified, package not in the repo). The sync worker is held for the whole export and is still killed past 120s. An error mid-stream truncates the download instead of returning a 500.

reader.closing_answer: Yes, implement streaming in app/exports.py. I first check the ferngrove package (web.Response and db) for iterator and cursor support and adapt to what exists. If either is missing, I report that back rather than silently switching approaches.
